findings.excerpt: John Patterson's 49 points at Littlestone was the third-best round in TEG history to date.
It was also, comfortably, the best round of his career.
He arrived at it from the bottom of the 2020 Wooden Spoon race, where he had been sitting for two rounds.
Round two had produced 28 points.
The swing between the two days was 21 points.
A bogey at the par-5 5th, one of the easier holes on the course, briefly dropped him back into last place in the Spoon standings mid-round.
briefly dropped him back into last place in the Spoon standings mid-round
He answered immediately, taking 13 points across holes 8 to 11, the highlight a par at the 10th, the hardest hole on the course.
the highlight a par at the 10th, the hardest hole on the course

findings.detail: claim type 'record' has no checker yet
findings.excerpt: Steady gross golf either side of that run delivered a personal-best gross score of +12.
A late quadruple bogey at the 17th did little to dent the total.
The round flipped the Wooden Spoon race outright, leaving Alex Baker rather than Patterson anchoring the bottom of the standings.
A round 100 at Littlestone did the damage.
Alex Baker opened with a double bogey at the 1st.
A second double bogey at the 3rd completed the set.
Three holes played, eight shots gone.
a triple bogey at the 8th, a double at the 9th and another double at the 10th

Seven more shots in three holes, the last of them on the hardest hole on the course.
